blocks.text: Modern systems combine VMs, containers and serverless: VMs give isolation and kernel control, containers give portable packaging and density, and serverless gives zero-ops, event-driven scaling. Most real stacks layer containers on VMs.

items: Container-based serverless (Cloud Run, Fargate, Container Apps): run an OCI image without managing servers.
MicroVMs (Firecracker, Kata) give containers VM-grade isolation; Lambda runs on Firecracker.
WebAssembly is emerging for very lightweight sandboxed workloads.

blocks.text: Containers for the API, workers, Postgres/pgvector and the vector DB (local and prod), a managed database in production where possible, GPU VMs for model serving, and serverless for event-driven ingestion if it fits.

Q: "When would you choose a VM, a container or serverless?" A: "VMs when you need a specific kernel/OS or strong tenant isolation; containers for portable, dense, long-running services; serverless for event-driven, spiky workloads where zero ops matters more than control. In practice containers run on VMs, and container-based serverless blurs the line."

items: VMs, containers and serverless are layers, not rivals.
Container-based serverless runs OCI images without servers.
Choose by isolation, control and scaling needs.
